```{r knitr-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,

library(vayuayan)
```

For each sensor, [OAQ](https://oaq.notf.in) supplies the 15-minute readings of
each day. It also supplies one daily value for each day (in the annual and
monthly files). The usual definition of a daily value is the mean of the
readings of that day.

This article shows that the daily value is the mean until the last days of
February 2026. From approximately 1 March 2026, the daily value is usually the
**last 15-minute reading of the day**. The date of the change is not the same
for all sensors, but the differences are small. We see the change on all three
providers (`cpcb`, `airnet`, `aurassure`), in Bengaluru, Delhi and Cuttack. For
daily means from March 2026, use `oaq_daily_means()`.

The Python notebook *OAQ daily values* does this analysis again with the same
functions. For the OAQ calls, you must have `OAQ_API_KEY`.

```{r setup}
session <- oaq_session()
change <- "2026-03-01"
labels <- c(
  "cpcb 164" = "cpcb 164 · Bengaluru",
  "cpcb 103" = "cpcb 103 · Delhi",
  "airnet 12036" = "airnet 12036 · Bengaluru",
  "airnet 12096" = "airnet 12096 · Bengaluru",
  "aurassure 14709" = "aurassure 14709 · Cuttack"
)
```

# One day in detail

This section uses `cpcb` sensor 103 (CRRI Mathura Road, Delhi) on 7 March
2026. `oaq_check_daily_records()` compares the daily value of OAQ (`record`)
with the statistics of the readings of that day.

```{r one-day}
check <- oaq_check_daily_records(session, "cpcb", "103", "2026-03-07")
check[, c("date", "record", "n", "mean", "last", "max", "last_2_mean", "class")]
```

```{r one-day-plot}
plot_daily_record_day(
  oaq_readings(session, "cpcb", "103", "2026-03-07"), check,
  title = "cpcb 103 (Delhi), 7 March 2026"
)
```

The daily value is equal to the 23:45 reading. It is not the mean of the
readings of that day, the maximum, or the mean of the last two readings. A day
in Bengaluru shows the same result:

```{r second-day}
plot_daily_record_day(
  oaq_readings(session, "cpcb", "164", "2026-05-29"),
  oaq_check_daily_records(session, "cpcb", "164", "2026-05-29"),
  title = "cpcb 164 (Bengaluru), 29 May 2026"
)
```

# All days of six sensor-years

`oaq_audit_daily_records()` examines each complete day of the specified sensors
and years. It does not include today, because the values for today are not
complete.

```{r audit}
audit <- rbind(
  oaq_audit_daily_records(session, data.frame(provider = "cpcb", sensor_id = "164"), c(2025, 2026)),
  oaq_audit_daily_records(
    session,
    data.frame(
      provider = c("cpcb", "airnet", "airnet", "aurassure"),
      sensor_id = c("103", "12036", "12096", "14709")
    ),
    2026
  )
)
nrow(audit)
table(paste(audit$provider, audit$sensor_id), audit$class)
```

`daily_record_summary()` counts the days on which the mean and the last reading
have a difference of more than 1. On these days, a value cannot agree with the
two statistics accidentally. The function also finds when each sensor changed.
It gives the last day with a value equal to only the mean. It also gives the
first day with a value equal to only the last reading.

```{r summary}
daily_record_summary(audit)
```

```{r timeline, fig.height = 4}
plot_daily_record_timeline(audit, change = change, labels = labels)
```

```{r scatter, fig.height = 6.4}
plot_daily_record_scatter(audit)
```

The days with a daily value equal to the mean (blue) are on the 1:1 line on
the left. The days with a daily value equal to the last reading (orange) are on
the 1:1 line on the right.

```{r share}
plot_daily_record_share(audit, change = change)
```

```{r series}
plot_daily_record_series(
  audit, "103",
  change = change,
  title = "cpcb 103 (Delhi): OAQ's daily value against the daily mean"
)
```

```{r difference}
plot_daily_record_difference(audit, change, labels = labels)
```

# Other explanations

The table that follows gives the number of days on which the daily value is
equal to each statistic of the readings. The statistics are the mean, the last
reading, the maximum, the median, and the mean of the last 2 and the last 4
readings (a mean over a short period at the end of the day).

```{r statistics}
stats <- grep("^record_is_", names(audit), value = TRUE)
aggregate(audit[stats], audit[c("provider", "sensor_id")], sum, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# Notes

- This article examines only `pm25`, and five sensors on three providers.
- Some daily values are not equal to the mean or to the last reading. Most of
  these values are for Aurassure 14709 from August 2026. We cannot identify
  these values.


- `monthly_2026_03.json` returns HTTP 404 for `cpcb` 103 and `cpcb` 164, but
  `annual_2026.json` has the data for March.
